What the radio slot's bind orchestrates: each radio joins the rating's roving group (api.internal.roving.bind) while it's mounted, with a native element the order twin sorts in render order and the host focuses.

What the item slot's bind orchestrates: each item joins the control's roving group (api.internal.roving.bind) while it's mounted, with a native element the order twin sorts in render order and the host focuses.

What the button, link and input slots' bind orchestrates: each item joins the toolbar (api.internal.join) while it's mounted, so the toolbar lists its items in render order, keeps its stop on an enabled one and its controller focuses it.

What the root slot's bind orchestrates: the toggle joins its group (api.internal.join) while its root is mounted, so the group lists its toggles in render order, refuses a disabled one and focuses one.

What the tab slot's bind orchestrates: a tab joins the roving group (api.internal.roving.bind) while it's mounted, so the tabs know their tabs in render order, select the first enabled one and focus the selected one. The disclosure trigger and panel it shares with Collapsible need nothing more on native: a Pressable is always a button and the OS activates it, find in page and the panel's tab stop don't exist, and the panel's exit is the adapter's presence.

What the panel slot's bind orchestrates through bindPanel: the panel settles (api.internal.settled) when the adapter's presence does, at once on opening and once onExit's done ends a close, through presence-native.ts's onSettled. The size variables become the panel's measured size in the adapter's state (src/disclosure-panel.tsx), and the exiting flag stays the adapter's presence.

What the root and label slots' bind orchestrates for Progress and Meter: the root reads the page's locale through bindPageLocale while it's mounted, which the locale twin will answer from Intl, and a mounted label counts toward the root's aria-labelledby (api.internal.label).
The controller's focus() calls focusPart instead of element("trigger")?.focus(), and the api reads parts from its context.

Reads the direction from the native host (I18nManager.isRTL) for the whole app, ignoring the element, where the DOM module reads the element's computed direction. There's no browser, so isBrowser and isIOS are false.
The page's and the user's language are the device's, from Intl, where the DOM module reads the nearest lang attribute and navigator.languages.

What the root's bind, the control's pointerdown and the thumb input's input event orchestrate: the root reads the locale, the control follows the responder's touches with begin, move and end (measured on the track), cancelling on a cancelled, taken or unmounted responder, and each thumb takes a screen reader's increment and decrement as an adjustment.
The controller's focus() calls focusPart instead of the thumb input's focus(). Additive: internal.cancel(), which puts the value back and commits nothing, and adjust()'s event is optional.

The layer stack with no document: the same stack, order, nesting and persistent layers, with back, the escape gesture and a backdrop press coming from the native host's listen and going to the topmost layer (a backdrop press down to the first shielding one), where the DOM module listens to the document. Its Layer widens the DOM's with onBack, onEscapeGesture and onBackdropPress, which take no event.

A closing popup with no element stays mounted while its content's view holds it, and unmounts once the adapter's presence ends the content's exit, where popup.ts waits for the element's animations through animateOut.

What popup.bind's attach orchestrates: pushing and popping the layer and running the onShow rule while the popup is open, back, escape and outside press through the host's input as requestClose, the focus request on open by the opener's plan and on close by the close's focus mode, starting at the trigger. The trigger, title and description slots set the trigger key and the titled and described flags their bind sets. The content holds the popup mounted until its exit ends. pressTrigger passes the opener a native press stands for.

Dialog's focus on open (the title, or an alert dialog's first Close part when preferredFocus's auto applies), restated since preferredFocus reads elements, and its Escape rule: a non-modal dialog closes on the escape gesture only when it reached its content, where onEscape asks whether focus is inside the element.

The ADR's two popup.ts changes: the unmount on close of a popup with no element goes through motion/exit.ts's afterExit and mountedAs asks its holdsMount (both at once on the DOM host), and closeFocus() reads the focus mode of the close under way.
The ADR's popup-features.ts change: a trigger press takes its opener from the caller, defaulting to openerOf(event).
The controller's focus() calls focusPart instead of triggerElement()?.focus().
Exports popupNative and partIn, which Dialog's native behavior file imports.

What the root's and the day's bind orchestrate: the root reads the locale and today through bindRoot, and each day joins the roving group with a native element the order twin sorts and the host focuses.
Hermes's Intl has no Intl.Locale, so the first day of the week comes from the tag's region and CLDR's table, where the DOM module asks Intl.Locale's week info and maximizes the tag.
Hermes's Intl.DateTimeFormat has no formatRange, so a range of dates is its two dates joined by a dash, where the DOM module formats it with formatRange.
A 30 second timeout: the type program it builds took about 6 seconds after Calendar (#102) merged, over Vitest's 5 second default.

Budgets for @ui-sdk/react-native/primitive, switch, button, checkbox, collapsible, accordion, toggle, avatar, radio, rating, segmented-control, tabs, testing, input, textarea, password-input, otp-input, slider, dialog, alert-dialog, popover, file-input, overlays and toast.

What the item and panel slots' bind orchestrate: an item registers with a stand-in from nativeElement, so the items' order comes from the order twin; a panel settles (api.internal.settled(key, open)) when the adapter's presence does, through presence-native.ts's onSettled, as collapsible-native.ts does. The size variables become the panel's measured size in the adapter's state (src/disclosure-panel.tsx), and the exiting list stays the adapter's presence.

The items' order sorts the registered items with inDocumentOrder instead of reading elements(context, "item"), so the order twin sorts native stand-ins; the controller's focus() calls focusPart, with the first item's key when no value is given.
No page styles on the native host: ahead, afterPaint and the style writers do nothing, so a popup preset's placement.prepare never reaches performance or CSS.

Placement on the native host: what position() writes (the side, align, available and anchor sizes, transform origin and arrow offset on the popup; the arrow's offset, side, align and clamped flag), computed with the shared computePlacement, computeArrow, arrowOffset and transformOrigin from boxes the adapter measures in the host's coordinates, with the options placementOptions resolves from the content's props as bindPopupContent does.

Popover's focus on open: the title, where pressOpening's initialFocus picks the first focusable element, and the content after a touch or with initialFocus="content", as the DOM host focuses the popup itself.

What the content's bind adds to a popup's: it joins the warm group while mounted. Its Escape rule for the screen reader's escape gesture: a tooltip never takes focus, so when the gesture reached its text the screen reader goes back to the trigger, where the DOM host's focus never left it.

Hover Card's content bind is a plain popup's: the layer, back, escape, outside press and the exit, which popup-native.ts restates; a hover open moves no focus, as initialFocusPlan("hover") says on the DOM host.
checkEvent skips an event that isn't a DOM Event, like the pointer event React Native hands a tooltip's hover.
Exports transformOrigin, which placement-native.ts imports through platform/index.ts.
Exports anchorRect, arrowOffset, computeArrow, computePlacement and transformOrigin, which popups/placement-native.ts imports.

Exports userLocale and createFolder, which the native agent bridge folds labels with.
Reads a core source export that is a condition object, like ./agent's, by its default target.

The sheet on the native host: the shared machine, snap points and physics driven by one finger the host feeds it and moving a view the host owns (nativeSheet's bridge), where the DOM module measures elements, listens to pointers, writes translate and plays WAAPI animations. At a scroll view's start it takes the touch and scrolls the content itself, as the pointer driver does. Under reduced motion an open or close fades and a snap eases, as the pointer driver does; the host avoids the keyboard and steps stacked sheets back. Theme color and the scroll-snap driver are left out.
What the content's bind orchestrates: the sheet attached before the popup layer shows, and Dialog's focus and Escape rules; the handle's arrow keys as a screen reader's increment and decrement.

Where the native sheet and the host meet: the host's view (sizes, moves, the spring or the reduced-motion fade, and whether motion is reduced) and the finger it feeds the sheet, the native counterpart of the DOM driver boundary.

What the content's, the root's and the days' bind orchestrate: the popup's layer, focus in and back and exit through popupNative, with focus on open going to the day with the calendar's tab stop, as initialFocus picks it on the DOM host; the root reads the locale and today through bindRoot, and each day joins the roving group. datePickerText gives the native input the text the input's bind writes into the element.

internal spreads the popup kit's internals under Calendar's, so popupNative and placeNative read the preset, parts, rules and trigger slot as they do on Popover; focusInput calls focusPart with the start input, so Clear and a Field's label focus the native input through the focus twin.

open() calls the pick function the app passes to the root, and hands the files it returns to the checks with the picker reason, where the web clicks the hidden <input type="file"> and its change event hands them over. A canceled pick reports nothing, as a canceled picker doesn't on the web.

The agent bridge reads each part from what the adapter rendered, through the native host's seen, and presses its view's press, where the DOM module reads and clicks elements. registerTools does nothing: there is no browser agent.

The registry installs without a document and names a component from what its parts' views read, through the native host's seen, where the DOM module reads elements, their type and autocomplete. Native views have no rows.
Keeps the instances made before a watcher without checking for a document, which the DOM module does to leave a server's instances alone.
open() calls openPicker from file-input-picker.ts, which has a native twin, instead of clicking input() itself, and the controller's focus() calls focusPart instead of element("trigger")?.focus().

The scroll area's engine on the native host (scroll-area-native.ts): the host reports the ScrollView's scroll events and layouts and scrolls it, where the DOM view measures the viewport, observes its size and writes CSS variables. Its DOM binds do nothing.

What the viewport's, scrollbars' and thumbs' binds orchestrate: edges, overflow, scrolling and visibility flags from the reported scroll position, sticking to the end as the content grows, the controller's scrolls, and a scrollbar touch that drags the thumb or pages, with the thumb's geometry handed to the host instead of CSS variables. A drag held near the viewport's edge scrolls it a step at a time (edgeScroll), at auto-scroll.ts's speeds.

Additive: drag(key), the decisions pointerdown's handler makes (pick up as a pointer, place by the items' boxes, drop with the drag reason or put back), followed through point-drag.ts with edge scrolling, for a drag that doesn't start with pointerdown, like a native touch. An item's default label goes through item-label.ts, which has a native twin, instead of labelOf.

The pointer drag's placing moves out of pointerdown into place(key, x, y), unchanged. Additive: drag(key), as reorder.ts's, through point-drag.ts, for a drag that doesn't start with pointerdown, like a native touch. An item's default label goes through item-label.ts, which has a native twin, instead of labelOf.
A moving item the app doesn't label is announced by its key, where labelOf reads the element's text, which core can't read from a native view.

Scrolls only the library's Scroll Areas under the finger, through the host's scrollNear and each viewport's edgeScroll, once per frame while it's near an edge, where the DOM module scrolls any scrollable element and the window.

What a reorderable item's and a transfer's list and item binds and pointerdown orchestrate: each joins with a stand-in, and the responder's touches pick the item up past the drag threshold, follow it with drag(key), and drop it, or put it back on a cancelled, taken or unmounted responder. A transfer's list holds the touch, since an item moved to another list is a new view.

What a toast's bind and pointerdown orchestrate for a swipe: the responder's touches become a swipe along an axis with a direction past a few points (also when a button inside took the touch), the timers pause while it runs, and its release dismisses with the swipe reason or snaps back, by the web's distance and velocity rules; the offset goes to the host through nativeToast instead of CSS variables.

button.root.reason: Its bind reads what element it rendered as and a disabled fieldset, neither of which exists on native: the part stays unknown, whose type="button" the translation makes the button role. Its keydown and keyup activate a non-button element, where the OS activates the Pressable with Space or Enter.

radioGroup.group.reason: Its bind makes the group take part in a form and focuses a radio from a label pointing at the group, neither of which native has. Its focus is the api's, through the radios that joined.

radioGroup.root.reason: Its bind joins the roving group, which radio-native.ts does while the radio is mounted, and names it from a label, which native names from its text or aria-label. Its keydown and keyup move between radios with arrow keys and check one with Space, which native doesn't build, and the OS activates the Pressable. Its mousedown keeps a disabled radio from taking focus, which a disabled view never takes on native.

radioGroup.input.reason: The hidden input part isn't rendered on native, which has no forms.

rating.root.reason: Its bind makes the rating take part in a form and focuses it from a label, which native doesn't have. Its pointermove previews a score under a mouse and ignores touch, like upstream's touch behavior, and native's presses come from touch.

rating.radio.reason: Its bind joins the rating's roving group, which rating-native.ts does while the radio is mounted, and names it from a label, which native names with aria-label. Its keydown and keyup move between stars with arrow keys and check one with Space, which native doesn't build, and the OS activates the Pressable.

rating.input.reason: The hidden input part isn't rendered on native, which has no forms.

meter.root.reason: Its bind reads the page's language, which gauge-native.ts asks for as the root mounts; until the locale twin lands it reads none and formats in English unless the locale option is given. Its missing-name warning comes with the names work.

meter.label.reason: Its bind counts the label that names the root, which gauge-native.ts does while the label is mounted.

progress.root.reason: Its bind reads the page's language, which gauge-native.ts asks the locale twin for as the root mounts: the device's language, unless the locale option is given. Its missing-name warning comes with the names work.

progress.label.reason: Its bind counts the label that names the root, which gauge-native.ts does while the label is mounted.

segmentedControl.root.reason: Its bind makes the control take part in a form and focuses an item from a label pointing at the control, neither of which native has. Its focus is the api's, through the items that joined.

segmentedControl.item.reason: Its bind joins the roving group, which segmented-control-native.ts does while the item is mounted, and names it from a label, which native names from its text or aria-label. Its keydown and keyup move between items with arrow keys and check one with Space, which native doesn't build, and the OS activates the Pressable. Its mousedown keeps a disabled item from taking focus, which a disabled view never takes on native.

segmentedControl.input.reason: The hidden input part isn't rendered on native, which has no forms.

segmentedControl.indicator.reason: Its bind measures the checked item against the control and writes the --segmented-control-indicator-* variables; SegmentedControlIndicator measures them from the layouts of the control and its items and hands them to its state.

switchPrimitive.root.reason: Its press is the adapter's generic press, its focus() goes through the focus-part twin, and it takes part in no form.

switchPrimitive.input.reason: The hidden input part isn't rendered on native, which has no forms.

input.root.reason: Its bind follows typing and writes; the TextInput's onChangeText goes through the api's change, and its value prop follows the state, which puts a canceled edit back.

textarea.root.reason: Its bind is the text field's, as for input.root. Its keydown runs the submit shortcut, which is absent: Enter adds a line and TextInput reports no modifiers. A multiline TextInput grows with its text unless its style fixes a height.

inputGroup.group.reason: Its bind reads the field's state from the DOM; the field inside the group reports it with api.internal.update and registers itself as the field the native host's field(part) returns.

collapsible.root.reason: Its bind watches a disabled fieldset, which doesn't exist on native.

collapsible.trigger.reason: Its bind gives a non-button element the button role and a tab stop, and its keydown activates it with Enter and Space; a Pressable is always a button the OS activates. Its press is the adapter's generic press, and its focus() goes through the focus-part twin.

collapsible.panel.reason: Its bind settles the panel after its animations, which collapsible-native.ts does when the adapter's presence settles; writes the size variables, which CollapsiblePanel measures into its state (src/disclosure-panel.tsx); keeps it findable, which native has no find in page for; and moves focus out of a panel closing around it, which native never observes.

checkbox.input.reason: The hidden input part isn't rendered on native, which has no forms.

checkboxGroup.group.reason: Its bind makes the group take part in a form, which native doesn't have. Its focus is the api's, through the checkboxes that joined.

checkboxGroup.group-input.reason: The hidden input part isn't rendered on native, which has no forms.

toolbar.root.reason: Its bind marks the toolbar bound, which only tells a server render a button from other elements, and watches a disabled fieldset, which the adapter hands down through DisabledContext. Its keydown moves between items with arrow keys, Home and End, which native doesn't build.

toolbar.button.reason: Its bind joins the toolbar, which toolbar-native.ts does while the button is mounted; the element it records is always a Pressable on native, and the presses and keys it refuses on a disabled item are refused by the Pressable's disabled. Its keydown and keyup activate a non-button element, where the OS activates the Pressable.

toolbar.link.reason: Its bind joins the toolbar, which toolbar-native.ts does while the link is mounted; the presses it refuses on a disabled link are refused by the Pressable's disabled.

toolbar.input.reason: Its bind joins the toolbar, which toolbar-native.ts does while the field is mounted. The arrow keys it leaves to the caret aren't built on native, and ToolbarInput in packages/react-native/src/toolbar.tsx stops a disabled field from being edited.

toggle.root.reason: Its bind joins the toggle's group, which toggle-native.ts does while the root is mounted; the element it records and a disabled fieldset don't exist on native. Its keydown and keyup activate a non-button element, where the OS activates the Pressable, and move between toggles with arrow keys, which native doesn't build.

toggle.icon.reason: Its bind flips a mirrored icon right to left, which the translation does when the app runs right to left. The data-has-icon marks it writes on the toggle and the group have no state field, and its missing-name warning comes with the names work.

toggleGroup.group.reason: Its bind watches a disabled fieldset, which doesn't exist on native.

field.root.reason: Its bind reads validity, watches fieldsets and focus, and follows submit and reset. field-native.ts marks the field bound; native computes no validity and has no form; the FieldSet around it hands its disabled state down through the adapter (DisabledContext in use-primitive.tsx); the field's focused state isn't followed.

field.label.reason: Its bind registers its id, which field-native.ts does while it's mounted. Its press goes through the label-press twin.

field.description.reason: Its bind registers its id, which field-native.ts does while it's mounted.

field.error.reason: Its bind registers its id, which field-native.ts does, and announces its text when it appears or changes, which Field in packages/react-native/src/field.tsx does from the error's registered plain text.

field.control.reason: Its bind records the control's id for a native <label for>, which native doesn't have; controls join the field through useFieldControl in packages/react-native/src/field-context.ts.

fieldSet.set.reason: Its bind watches a disabled fieldset around it; FieldSet reads the one around it from the adapter's DisabledContext and hands its own down.

fieldSet.legend.reason: Its bind registers its id for the set's aria-labelledby, which names a container, and native never labels a container.

fieldSet.description.reason: Its bind registers its id for the set's aria-describedby, which describes a container, and native never describes a container.

tabs.list.reason: Its keydown moves between tabs with arrow keys, Home and End, which native doesn't build, and activates a non-button tab, where the OS activates the Pressable.

tabs.tab.reason: Its bind joins the roving group, which tabs-native.ts does while the tab is mounted; the element it records is always a button on native.

tabs.tab-icon.reason: Its bind flips a mirrored icon right to left, which the translation does when the app runs right to left. The data-has-icon marks it writes on the tab and the list have no state field, and its missing-name warning comes with the names work.

tabs.indicator.reason: Its bind measures the selected tab against the list and writes the --active-tab-* variables; TabsIndicator measures them from the layouts of the list and its tabs and hands them to its state.

tabs.panel.reason: Its bind animates the panel in and out, which the adapter's presence does through onExit. It also points tabs' aria-controls at it, keeps it findable and makes it a tab stop, none of which exists on native.

passwordInput.control.reason: Its bind is the text field's, whose onChangeText goes through the api's change and whose value prop follows the state, and switches the field between text and password, which the translation does with secureTextEntry from the type attribute. It also hides the password before a form submits or resets and when the page is hidden, and follows a disabled fieldset, none of which exists on native. Its keydown, keyup and mousedown read Caps Lock, which TextInput doesn't report, so capsLock stays false; its focusout keeps the selection for a mouse press on the toggle, and on native a press on the toggle leaves the field focused.

passwordInput.toggle.reason: Its bind records the element, which is always a button on native. Its mousedown keeps focus in the field, which a Pressable never takes on native, and its keydown and keyup activate a non-button element, where the OS activates the Pressable.

label.root.reason: Its bind finds the control by htmlFor or inside the label and writes the label's id into the control's aria-labelledby. Label registers its id for its htmlFor (names.ts), and the control that joins through useFieldControl in field-context.ts takes it as its aria-labelledby and registers what a press activates by its id. Its press looks the control up in the document, so Label presses the control registered for its htmlFor; a disabled one ignores it. Its mousedown keeps a double click from selecting the label's text, which a Text never does.

otpInput.control.reason: Its bind follows the <input>'s typing, paste, selection, focus and blur, which the TextInput's onChangeText, onSelectionChange, onFocus and onBlur hand to internal.typeText, selectText and focusText, and its value and selection props follow the state. A press on a slot calls internal.pressSlot. Arrow keys, Home and End, which TextInput doesn't report, the browser's undo history, a restored page, form reset, a disabled fieldset, password managers' badges and the selection stylesheet have no native counterpart.
